title: At the Doctor's Office
target_phrases: I need to see a doctor
I have a pain in my...
How long have you felt this way?

dialogue.title: Ahmed's Medical Checkup
dialogue.context: Ahmed visits a doctor because he's been feeling sick. He describes his symptoms and the doctor examines him.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning! Do you have an appointment?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes, I'm Ahmed Hassan. I have a 10 AM appointment with Dr. Chen.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Perfect. Please fill out this form with your medical history and insurance information.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Okay, thank you. [After 10 minutes] Here's the completed form.

lines.speaker: Nurse
lines.text: Ahmed? Come with me. Let me check your blood pressure and temperature first. What brings you in today?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I've had a bad cough for two weeks. Also, my throat is very sore.

lines.speaker: Dr. Chen
lines.text: Hello Ahmed, I'm Dr. Chen. I hear you've had a cough. How long have you felt this way?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: It started about two weeks ago. At first it was just a small cough, but now it's much worse.

lines.speaker: Dr. Chen
lines.text: I see. Do you have any fever? Any chest pain when you breathe?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I had a fever last week, but not anymore. Sometimes my chest hurts when I cough hard.

lines.speaker: Dr. Chen
lines.text: Let me listen to your lungs. Take a deep breath... Good. I think you have bronchitis. I'll prescribe antibiotics. Take them twice a day for 10 days. Don't stop early even if you feel better.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Should I take any other medicine for the cough?

lines.speaker: Dr. Chen
lines.text: Yes, you can take over-the-counter cough syrup. Also, drink lots of water and rest. If you're not better in 3-4 days, call us.

listening_exercises.transcript: When describing symptoms to a doctor, be specific. Instead of saying 'I don't feel good,' say 'I have a sharp pain in my lower back that's worse in the morning.' Tell your doctor when symptoms started, how often they occur, and what makes them better or worse. This helps the doctor diagnose you correctly.
listening_exercises.question: What should you tell your doctor about your symptoms?
options: Just say you don't feel good
Be specific about location, timing, and severity
Wait for the doctor to guess

listening_exercises.transcript: Common symptoms vocabulary: 'fever' means high body temperature, usually over 100.4°F. 'Nausea' means feeling like you might vomit. 'Dizzy' means feeling like the room is spinning. 'Fatigue' means extreme tiredness. 'Congestion' means your nose is blocked. Learn these words to communicate with doctors effectively.
listening_exercises.question: What does 'nausea' mean?

listening_exercises.transcript: After your appointment, make sure you understand your treatment plan. Ask questions if anything is unclear. Before leaving, confirm: What medicines should I take? How often? For how long? What should I avoid? When should I call if I don't feel better? Can I go to work or school? It's okay to ask the doctor to repeat or write down instructions.
listening_exercises.question: What should you do if you don't understand the doctor's instructions?

speaking_tasks.prompt: You're at the doctor. Describe these symptoms: bad headache for 3 days, fever yesterday, very tired. Record for 25 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: Hello doctor. I've had a really bad headache for three days now. It's a throbbing pain on both sides of my head. Yesterday I also had a fever - my temperature was 101 degrees. I've been feeling very tired and weak. The headache gets worse when I move around. I took ibuprofen but it only helped a little bit. I'm worried because this headache won't go away.

speaking_tasks.prompt: The doctor says: 'Take this medicine twice a day for 7 days.' Ask 3 follow-up questions. Record yourself.
speaking_tasks.example: Thank you, doctor. I have a few questions to make sure I understand. First, should I take this medicine with food or on an empty stomach? Second, what time of day should I take it - morning and evening? And third, what should I do if I forget to take a dose? Also, are there any side effects I should watch for?

writing_tasks.prompt: Describe a time you were sick. What were your symptoms? What did you do? Did you see a doctor? (60-80 words)
writing_tasks.example: Last winter, I got a really bad flu. I had a high fever, terrible body aches, and a cough that wouldn't stop. I felt so weak I could barely get out of bed. After three days, I went to see a doctor because I wasn't getting better. She examined me and prescribed antiviral medication and cough syrup. She told me to rest and drink lots of fluids. It took about a week, but I finally recovered. Now I get a flu shot every year to prevent getting sick again.

writing_tasks.prompt: You need to call your doctor's office to make an appointment. Write what you would say on the phone. (40-50 words)
writing_tasks.example: Hello, my name is Ahmed Hassan. I'm a patient of Dr. Chen. I need to make an appointment because I've had a bad cough for two weeks and it's not getting better. Do you have any availability this week? I'm available any afternoon after 2 PM. Thank you.

grammar_focus.title: Present Perfect for Duration (I've had...)
grammar_focus.explanation: Use present perfect to describe symptoms that started in the past and continue now.
examples: I've had this cough for two weeks. (started 2 weeks ago, still have it)
She's felt dizzy since Monday. (started Monday, still feels it)
He's been sick for three days. (3 days ago until now)
We've had these symptoms since yesterday. (started yesterday, continue)

practice.sentence: I ___ had a headache for 3 days.

grammar_focus.title: Imperatives for Medical Instructions
grammar_focus.explanation: Doctors use imperative (command) form to give instructions.
examples: Take this medicine twice a day. (command)
Drink lots of water. (instruction)
Rest for a few days. (advice)
Don't stop the antibiotics early. (negative command)

grammar_focus.title: 'Should' for Medical Advice
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'should' to ask for or give medical recommendations.
examples: Should I take this with food? (asking for advice)
You should rest today. (giving advice)
Should I come back next week? (asking recommendation)
You shouldn't lift heavy things. (advising against)

vocabulary.example: Fever is a common symptom of the flu.

vocabulary.definition: coverage that pays for medical care
vocabulary.example: My health insurance covers doctor visits.

cultural_notes: In the U.S., you usually need to make an appointment to see a doctor. Emergency rooms are for serious emergencies only.
Bring your insurance card and photo ID to every doctor visit.
Most doctors' offices charge a 'copay' - a small amount you pay at each visit, usually $20-50.
It's normal to wait 10-30 minutes past your appointment time. Bring something to read.
You have the right to ask questions and get clear explanations about your health.
If you don't understand medical terms, ask the doctor to explain in simpler words.
